title: The harness: session, hooks and store
bridge: nova-worker is like a small Node service run by pm2: it starts, reads its config, and does one long job. Except the job is a Claude session that runs tools on the VM. Our code only sets the options, the walls and where the transcript is saved. It never limits turns, time or budget.
intro: nova-worker is the program that runs inside every sandbox VM. This lesson writes its three core files. session.ts starts a Claude Agent SDK session that talks only to our LLM gateway. hooks.ts holds the walls. store.ts saves the transcript to S3 so a run can resume on another VM.

picture.caption: nova-worker sets up one session. The model's calls go through the gateway; hooks guard every tool; the transcript leaves the VM batch by batch.

steps.text: systemd starts nova-worker run /run/nova/task.json as user agent
query() with our options; the SDK runs the pinned claude binary
every model call carries the run token; the gateway adds the real key
before each tool and before stopping, the hooks may refuse
ask_human, post_progress, kb_search refresh, and a heartbeat every 30 s
each transcript batch is PUT through a URL the broker presigned

p: The harness lives in ai-agents/harness/src/. main.ts is the command, nova-worker run /run/nova/task.json, behind a #!/usr/bin/env node line. session.ts builds the options, tools.ts holds our three tools, hooks.ts the walls, and store.ts the session store. It ships as one bundled file (lesson g3-1) and runs as user agent under systemd (lesson g3-8).
Because it is a bundle, it imports the SDK from @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/core, the entry the SDK documents for bundled apps. The names are the same as the root entry.

main.ts puts the gateway URL and the run token into process.env at start. Every session in the VM then reaches the gateway the same way: Nova, the QA agent, judges and reviewers. It writes /run/nova/status.json (step, state, session_id, result). A setInterval timer sends a heartbeat to the broker every 30 seconds. The model runs in the claude subprocess, so a long thinking turn still counts as alive.

sections.h: The options, part 1: model, tools, permissions
p: Our three tools live in an in-process MCP server built with createSdkMcpServer and tool() (lesson p8-3). ask_human posts a question to the ticket's thread and ends the turn with status needs_answer. post_progress posts a short update. kb_search runs the kb search CLI from rnd-kb-tooling over a local rnd-kb mirror in $KB_DIR. Nova ranks pages exactly like people do.
sections.because: We list every allowed tool and use dontAsk, because nobody sits at a prompt in a VM.

code.text:
// ai-agents/harness/src/session.ts: sketch. No key in the VM: the gateway adds it.
import { createSdkMcpServer, type Options, type SessionStore } from "@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/core";

export const buildOptions = (task: Task, hooks: Options["hooks"], store: SessionStore): Options => {
  const route = routeFor(task.job); // Opus 5.5 at medium unless the plan picked another row (G3-33)
  return {
    model: route.model,
    effort: route.effort,
    cwd: "/work/fcp", // the same on every VM, so a stored session resumes anywhere
    settingSources: ["project"], // fcp's CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md and .claude/; managed settings load anyway
    allowedTools: ["Read", "Grep", "Glob", "Edit", "Write", "Bash", "TodoWrite",
      "Workflow", "mcp__nova__ask_human", "mcp__nova__post_progress", "mcp__nova__kb_search"], // Workflow: G4-09, G4-19
    disallowedTools: ["WebFetch", "WebSearch"], // the proxy blocks the web anyway; say so up front
    permissionMode: "dontAsk", // nobody sits at a prompt: anything not allowed is refused
    mcpServers: { nova: createSdkMcpServer({ name: "nova", tools: [askHuman, postProgress, kbSearch] }) }, // call the broker
    hooks, // walls (G3-21) and the progress watcher (G3-32)
    sessionStore: store, // transcripts to S3 through the broker (G3-23)
    resume: task.resumeSessionId, // after a question, or on a fresh VM
    pathToClaudeCodeExecutable: "/usr/local/bin/claude", // the pinned binary the nightly smoke test passed (G3-14)

notes.text: From /core, because the harness is bundled. Options and SessionStore are types only.
One function builds the options from the task, the hooks and the store, so tests can check them without starting a session.
The routing table (G3-33) picks model and effort per job. The default is Opus 5.5 at medium.
/work/fcp on every VM. The stored session's project key is built from cwd, so a different path would not resume.
Load fcp's own CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and .claude/ settings. Managed settings from the image load anyway.
The tools the model may use with no prompt. Workflow is there for the research and review-panel workflows (G4-09, G4-19).
MCP tool names are mcp__<server>__<tool>.
The web tools are denied outright. The proxy blocks the web anyway; saying so up front saves the model a wasted turn.
dontAsk: anything not allowed is refused, never sent to a person.
The hooks: the walls in this lesson and the progress watcher (G3-32).
Where the transcript is mirrored (section 6).
Set after a question was answered, or when the run moves to a fresh VM.
The pinned claude from the image, the exact binary the nightly smoke test passed (lesson g3-5).

sections.h: The options, part 2: no key in the VM
p: The env option replaces the claude subprocess's whole environment. So it spreads process.env first, then sets our values on top. Two settings point Claude Code at the gateway instead of Anthropic. The gateway checks the run token, adds the real key and meters the spend (G0-13).

The ticket also sets CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FINE_GRAINED_TOOL_STREAMING=1, which is off behind a gateway like tool search. With no API key, Claude Code cannot fetch feature flags. So the permission mode is set explicitly, and G4's W6 spike checks the Workflow tool works.
sections.because: We spread process.env before our values, because env replaces the environment, and a claude with no PATH or HOME cannot start.

notes.text: Keep PATH, HOME and the proxy variables from the image. Our values below win where names clash.
https://gateway.ai-agents.example.com:8443, reached over PrivateLink (lesson g3-3).
The run token: signed by the orchestrator, valid for this run only. It is not an Anthropic key.
stepEnv (G1-14) adds OTel tags and the x-ai-agents-step header. Agent, Jira key and run ride inside the token.
Tool search is off by default behind a gateway; we turn it back on.
A helper agent cannot start helpers of its own.
How many agents a workflow may run at once, by VM size: 3 on lite, 6 on full, 12 on wide.
The routing table's output limit and cache TTL.
The guide-don't-cage rule, written where the next person will see it.

callout.text: No maxTurns, no maxBudgetUsd, no taskBudget, no timer. Work is never cut off mid-run. Spend is watched at the gateway, and loops are caught by the progress watcher, not by a cap.

sections.h: Wall hooks, part 1: refuse and say why
p: Hooks are functions the SDK calls at fixed points (lesson p8-4). G3-21 adds three. PreToolUse refuses edits to protected paths and a few never-run commands. PostToolUse lints a file right after it is edited. Stop asks for proof before Nova may say done.

The protected paths come from ai-agents/settings/protected-paths.yaml, which release-harness.yml packs into the tarball. G0-18's locked-checks check reads the same file. It lists CI workflows, lint and type config, eval sets and the plan's QA checks. It is not a list in the prompt.
sections.because: We refuse with a calm reason and an alternative, because a model told only 'no' tries another way around.

notes.text: Types only, from /core. A hook is a plain async function of type HookCallback.
The globs for this repo's block of protected-paths.yaml, read once at start.
Never-run commands: infra apply or destroy, argocd app sync, gh workflow run, /dispatches, and the metadata address.
The input names the tool and its arguments. The matcher (Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit, or Bash) decides which calls reach us.
Edit and Write use file_path; NotebookEdit uses notebook_path.
The reason the model reads, with the alternative: add a new test, or ask the requester.
The same idea for Bash commands.
An empty object means 'no opinion': the normal permission rules decide.

callout.text: The real walls are elsewhere: no credentials in the VM, the broker's checks, GitHub refusing workflow edits without the workflows permission. The hook gives the model a clear answer and leaves a record.

sections.h: Wall hooks, part 2: evidence and the ledger
p: The Stop hook runs when the model wants to finish. fcp's own Stop hook (G7-14) already runs verify in this session, because settingSources loads fcp's project settings. So ours does not run it again. It checks that each check in the plan's QA plan has a passing run recorded after the last edit.

PostToolUse on Edit|Write runs the fast linter for that one file. That is biome check --write under frontend/, and black, isort and flake8 under cloud/, client/ and sdk/. Failures go back to the model as additionalContext.
sections.because: We let a stop through when the missing proof is not Nova's fault, because blocking on a flaky test loops forever.

notes.text: The plan's checks with no passing run after the last edit.
Nothing missing: allow the stop.
stop_hook_active means we already blocked once. If the gap is not Nova's (a flaky test, main red at freshen)...
...flag it as unproven, with the reason. It shows in the PR, and the loop ends.
Otherwise block, and tell the model exactly what to run and show.
Every refusal goes into the refusal ledger, /run/nova/refusals.jsonl, uploaded with the artifacts. G3-31 lists it in the PR.
The PreToolUse answer: deny, with the reason the model will read.

p: The VM is only a workbench. If the transcript lives only on its disk, a dead VM throws away the run's thinking. A SessionStore mirrors every transcript batch somewhere else (lesson p8-6). G3-23 copies Anthropic's TypeScript reference adapter, examples/session-stores/s3. It replaces its S3Client with broker-presigned URLs and fetch, because the VM has no AWS credentials.
Keys look like runs/<run_id>/sessions/<projectKey>/<sessionId>/[<subpath>/]part-<wall-clock ms>-<seq>.jsonl. Each append writes one new part file; nothing is ever rewritten.
sections.because: We name parts by wall-clock time, because a resumed run's counter starts at zero again on the new VM.

notes.text: The store types, from /core.
uuids of entries already stored. Retried batches can repeat entries, so we skip those.
A counter for parts written in the same millisecond.
The broker client is passed in, so tests can use a fake broker.
sessions/<projectKey>/<sessionId>, plus a subpath for a subagent's transcript. The broker adds runs/<run_id>/ in front.
Drop entries whose uuid we already stored.
part-<ms since 1970>-<6-digit counter>.jsonl. Names sort by time across VMs.
Ask the broker for a presigned PUT URL, then upload the entries as JSON lines.
On failure, throw. The SDK retries, then reports a mirror_error message.
Remember the uuids only after the upload succeeded.

sections.h: The store, part 2: load and subkeys
p: On resume the SDK calls load before the claude process even starts, so the new VM needs nothing on its disk. The workflow passes resume: <sessionId>, and cwd stays /work/fcp because the project key encodes it.
sections.because: We read the parts in name order, because name order is time order, and order matters in a conversation.

notes.text: The broker lists this run's objects with that prefix, sorted by name, which is time.
No parts: null tells the SDK there is nothing to resume.
Each part through a presigned GET URL from the broker.
Split into lines, drop empty ones, parse each as one entry.
listSubkeys lets subagent transcripts resume too.

callout.text: Leave enableFileCheckpointing off: the SDK refuses it together with a store. Watch for { type: "system", subtype: "mirror_error" } messages; count them and post_progress once if the store keeps failing. Retention is the bucket's 30-day expiry, because the SDK never deletes from a store.

quiz.q: A teammate writes env: { ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL: GATEWAY_URL, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN: token } without ...process.env. What happens?

options.text: Nothing changes: env is merged with the parent environment.
options.why: env replaces the subprocess environment. That is why the sketch spreads process.env first.

options.text: The claude subprocess starts with no PATH, HOME or proxy variables, and fails or cannot reach anything.
options.why: Only the two variables exist. Spreading process.env keeps the image's environment.

options.text: Claude Code falls back to an Anthropic key from the VM.
options.why: There is no key in the VM to fall back to. That is the wall.

quiz.q: Why must cwd be /work/fcp on every VM?

options.text: The stored session's project key is built from cwd; a different path would not find the session to resume.
options.why: Same path on every VM means a session stored on one VM resumes on any other.

options.text: Claude Code can only run inside a git checkout under /work.
options.why: It runs in any folder. The constraint comes from the session store's key.

options.text: The proxy allows file access only under /work.
options.why: The proxy filters network traffic, not files.

quiz.q: Nova wants to stop. One QA check never passed because a known flaky test fails, and stop_hook_active is true. What does requireEvidence do?

options.text: Blocks again, until the test passes.
options.why: That loops forever on a failure that is not Nova's. The hook is a wall for proof, not a cage.

options.text: Runs the flaky test itself until it passes.
options.why: The hook only checks the ledger. Running tests is the model's job, and fcp's Stop hook runs verify.

options.text: Allows the stop and flags the check as unproven, with the reason, in the PR.
options.why: ledger.notOurs(missing) is true, so it flags and lets go. A person sees the gap.

words.plain: The code around the model: nova-worker, which sets the options, tools, hooks and store for a session.
A token the orchestrator signs for one run. The gateway accepts it instead of an API key.
A permission mode: tools on the allowed list run, everything else is refused without a prompt.
The one list of files agents may not edit, read by the PreToolUse hook and by G0-18's check.
Part of a stored session's key, built from cwd, so the same cwd is needed to resume.
One JSON-lines file per append in the store, named by wall-clock time so parts sort across VMs.

Write /run/nova/status.json (step, state, session_id, result) and send a heartbeat to the broker every 30 s from a setInterval timer.

remember: The harness sets options, walls and a store, then gets out of the way: no key, no limits.
